LanguageData.LP_Undead_Abhorrent.label: abhorrent
LanguageData.LP_Undead_Abhorrent.description: The undead are a double blasphemy against life and death: lich revivals, creating necromantic constructs and draining souls are all disgusting. Every necromantic construct and every lich in the colony is unsettling.
LanguageData.LP_Undead_Wary.label: wary
LanguageData.LP_Undead_Wary.description: Necromancy is a dangerous power; it can be used, but with caution.
LanguageData.LP_Undead_Acceptable.label: acceptable
LanguageData.LP_Undead_Acceptable.description: Necromancy is just one school of magic, nothing special.
LanguageData.LP_Undead_Sacred.label: holy
LanguageData.LP_Undead_Sacred.description: Transcending death is the noblest pursuit. Lich revivals, creating necromantic constructs and draining souls are sacred acts; a phylactery in the colony is reassuring.
LanguageData.LP_Giants_Feared.label: feared
LanguageData.LP_Giants_Feared.description: Giants are walking disasters. Every giant-bodied colonist in the colony is unsettling (except for the giants themselves); killing a giant is a heroic feat.
LanguageData.LP_Giants_Respected.label: respected
LanguageData.LP_Giants_Respected.description: Giants are like any other race: some good, some bad.
LanguageData.LP_Giants_Supreme.label: supreme
LanguageData.LP_Giants_Supreme.description: Giants are born great, and smaller races should look up to them. Giant-bodied colonists get mood +3, other colonists -1; killing a giant is shameful.
LanguageData.LP_Arcane_Forbidden.label: forbidden
LanguageData.LP_Arcane_Forbidden.description: Magic is the root of corruption. Casting spells is shameful, and carrying magic items is unsettling.
LanguageData.LP_Arcane_Cautious.label: cautious
LanguageData.LP_Arcane_Cautious.description: Magic is a tool, to be used carefully. Feels a little uneasy after casting.
LanguageData.LP_Arcane_Revered.label: revered
LanguageData.LP_Arcane_Revered.description: Magic is a gift of the gods. Casting is pleasant; an enchanting table in the colony is reassuring.
LanguageData.LP_Arcane_Supreme.label: supremacy of the Weave
LanguageData.LP_Arcane_Supreme.description: Only those who master the Weave are whole. Casting is delightful; colonists who can't cast feel unfavored by the Weave. Only cultures with the "supremacy of the Weave" meme can pick this.
LanguageData.LP_Races_Human.label: human supremacy
LanguageData.LP_Races_Human.description: Only pure humans are masters of the world. Non-baseliner colonists get mood -2, baseliners +2. Can coexist with the vanilla "human primacy" meme.
LanguageData.LP_Races_Many.label: many peoples together
LanguageData.LP_Races_Many.description: Faerûn has always been a land where many peoples live together. Mood +3 when the colony has 4 or more xenotypes (city of many peoples).
LanguageData.LP_Races_Own.label: own people first
LanguageData.LP_Races_Own.description: Our people are the finest. Colonists of the culture's founding xenotype get mood +2, others -1. The founding xenotype is the most common xenotype among the colonists when the culture was first adopted by the player faction.
LanguageData.LP_Apotheosis_Blasphemy.label: blasphemous
LanguageData.LP_Apotheosis_Blasphemy.description: A mortal trying to become a god is blasphemy against the gods. Mood -4 when the colony has a demigod, -6 when the demigod ranks up.
LanguageData.LP_Apotheosis_Acceptable.label: acceptable
LanguageData.LP_Apotheosis_Acceptable.description: The gods too rose from among mortals.
LanguageData.LP_Apotheosis_Sacred.label: sacred mission
LanguageData.LP_Apotheosis_Sacred.description: Helping mortals become gods is our mission. Mood +6 when a demigod ranks up (witnessed a miracle); members of the same culture all count as the demigod's believers (+0.25 divine power per person per day).
LanguageData.LP_Offerings_None.label: no requirement
LanguageData.LP_Offerings_None.description: The gods need no mortal offerings.
LanguageData.LP_Offerings_Quarterly.label: quarterly offering
LanguageData.LP_Offerings_Quarterly.description: Each quarter (15 days) the colony must complete at least one offering at the altar (miracle fragments, silver or favored sacrifices); if not, mood -3 from day 16 (the god was not honored) until one is done. Divine favor from offerings under this precept ×1.5.
LanguageData.LP_Offerings_Blood.label: blood sacrifice
LanguageData.LP_Offerings_Blood.description: Evil gods love blood. The altar gets an extra "blood sacrifice" button: pick a prisoner to execute, and when done the patron deity gains +15 divine favor. Only available when the patron deity is an evil god.
